name: Greenhouse
tagline: The structured-hiring ATS most scaling tech companies standardize on.
bestFor: Companies of 200–5,000 employees that want structured interviews and a deep integration marketplace
pricing: Quote-based; three tiers (Essential, Advanced, Expert). Mid-market contracts commonly run $7,000–$30,000+ per year.
overview: Greenhouse popularised structured hiring: every role gets a scorecard, interview kits, and a defined plan, and reporting shows where the process leaks. Its marketplace of 500+ integrations means almost every tool on this site connects to it. The trade-off is price and a product that rewards process-mature teams more than tiny ones.
pros: Mature DE&I, compliance, and reporting features
Strong candidate experience and careers-page tooling
cons: Scheduling and CRM are add-ons or weaker than specialists
Reporting UI lags Ashby's built-in analytics

name: Lever
tagline: ATS plus built-in CRM for teams that nurture as much as they process.
bestFor: Mid-sized companies that want CRM nurture campaigns inside the ATS
pricing: Quote-based (LeverTRM and LeverTRM for Enterprise); typically $5,000–$25,000+ per year.
overview: Lever was the first mainstream ATS to merge the applicant tracker with a candidate relationship manager, so passive candidates, nurture emails, and pipeline live in one record. Now owned by Employ (alongside JazzHR and Jobvite), it remains a strong mid-market choice with a cleaner UI than Greenhouse and slightly fewer integrations.
pros: Native CRM, nurture sequences, and talent pools
cons: Product investment slowed after the Employ acquisition
Analytics require the enterprise tier or an add-on

name: Ashby
tagline: All-in-one ATS, scheduling, CRM, and analytics built for data-driven teams.
bestFor: Startups and scale-ups (20–2,000 employees) that want analytics and scheduling without extra tools
pricing: Published starting prices for small teams (Ashby Foundations) with per-employee pricing; mid-market and enterprise plans quote-based.
overview: Ashby has been the fastest-growing startup ATS since 2023 because it folds four purchases into one: tracking, interview scheduling, a sourcing CRM, and genuinely good analytics. Teams that previously ran Greenhouse + GoodTime + Gem + a BI tool often replace the lot. The marketplace is smaller and the product is opinionated.
pros: Best built-in analytics of any ATS
Native scheduling handles panel loops well
Transparent entry pricing for small teams
cons: Opinionated workflows can frustrate non-standard processes
Younger company; enterprise compliance features still maturing

name: Workable
tagline: Small-business ATS with job distribution, AI screening, and HR add-ons.
bestFor: Companies of 10–300 employees that want posting, tracking, and basic HR in one subscription
pricing: Published plans from roughly $149 per month (Starter) to $599+ per month (Premier), billed annually, plus optional HR and payroll modules.
overview: Workable is the easiest path from 'we post on LinkedIn and hope' to a real pipeline: one-click distribution to 200+ boards, AI-assisted screening and job descriptions, self-scheduling, and e-signature offers. It has added HRIS, time-off, and payroll modules, making it a plausible all-in-one for small companies.
pros: Fast setup and strong job-board distribution
AI screening and sourcing assist included
cons: Reporting and structured-interview depth below Greenhouse/Ashby
Per-job pricing tiers can get expensive for high-volume hiring
Sourcing database is shallow compared with dedicated tools

name: JazzHR
tagline: Budget ATS for small businesses that need pipeline and compliance basics.
bestFor: Small businesses hiring 5–50 people a year on a tight budget
pricing: Published plans from about $75 per month (Hero) to about $420 per month (Pro), billed annually.
overview: JazzHR (part of Employ) is one of the lowest-cost full ATS products: unlimited users, job distribution, custom workflows, e-signature offers, and EEO/OFCCP reporting. It lacks sophisticated analytics and sourcing, but for a small company it covers everything a spreadsheet cannot.
pros: Among the cheapest full-featured ATS plans
Good compliance reporting for the price
cons: Integration set is smaller than mid-market peers

name: Breezy HR
tagline: Visual, drag-and-drop ATS with a usable free plan.
bestFor: Small teams and nonprofits that want a free or low-cost pipeline
pricing: Free plan for one active job; paid plans from roughly $157 to $529 per month.
overview: Breezy HR's kanban pipeline, candidate self-scheduling, and video screening make it one of the friendliest small-business ATS products, and its free tier is genuinely usable for a single opening. Larger teams outgrow its reporting quickly.

name: SmartRecruiters
tagline: Enterprise talent-acquisition suite with marketplace and AI assistant.
bestFor: Global enterprises with thousands of hires a year and many hiring managers
pricing: Quote-based; priced per employee, typically six figures annually at enterprise scale.
overview: SmartRecruiters is an enterprise ATS and CRM suite with a consumer-grade hiring-manager experience, a large partner marketplace, and the Winston AI assistant for screening and scheduling. It competes with Workday Recruiting and iCIMS for global programs and is friendlier than either.
pros: Hiring-manager UX is unusually good for enterprise
Strong global compliance and multilingual support
cons: Reporting customization has a learning curve

name: iCIMS
tagline: Enterprise talent cloud for high-volume, high-compliance hiring.
bestFor: Large employers in retail, healthcare, and manufacturing with heavy compliance needs
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts, commonly six figures per year.
overview: iCIMS is one of the longest-standing enterprise ATS platforms, with modules for CRM, text recruiting, video, and offer management. It is chosen for configurability and compliance at scale rather than usability; implementations are substantial projects.
pros: Broad module set including text and video
cons: Interface feels dated next to modern suites

name: Bullhorn
tagline: The default ATS/CRM for staffing and recruiting agencies.
bestFor: Staffing agencies and recruitment firms with 10+ recruiters
pricing: Quote-based per-user licensing; commonly $100–$200 per user per month plus implementation.
overview: Bullhorn is built for the agency workflow: client companies, job orders, candidate submittals, placements, and back-office billing in one system. Its marketplace of staffing-specific integrations (VMS feeds, pay/bill, sourcing tools) is unmatched, which is why most sourcing tools advertise a Bullhorn sync.
pros: Agency-native data model (clients, job orders, placements)
Scales from boutique to global staffing firms
cons: Not designed for in-house corporate recruiting

name: Recruit CRM
tagline: Modern ATS + CRM for small and mid-sized recruiting agencies.
bestFor: Agencies with 2–50 recruiters that want transparent pricing and a modern UI
pricing: Published per-user plans from roughly $85 to $125+ per user per month.
overview: Recruit CRM combines applicant tracking, client CRM, email sequencing, and a Chrome sourcing extension in a product agencies can set up in a day. It is a common Bullhorn alternative for smaller firms that want published pricing and responsive support.
pros: Built-in email sequences and sourcing extension
cons: Reporting is adequate rather than deep

name: Loxo
tagline: Agency ATS/CRM with a built-in talent database and outreach.
bestFor: Executive-search and agency recruiters who want sourcing data inside the ATS
pricing: Free tier with limited features; published paid plans with per-user pricing.
overview: Loxo bundles an agency ATS/CRM with its own 1B+ profile database, contact finder, and outreach sequences, so recruiters can source and track in one place. Its free tier is a rare entry point for solo recruiters.
pros: Sourcing database and contact data built in
cons: Contact data quality varies by region
Enterprise agency features thinner than Bullhorn

name: Noon
tagline: Autonomous AI sourcing agent that finds candidates and runs personalized email and SMS outreach.
bestFor: In-house teams and agencies that want sourcing done end-to-end with recruiter approval, not another database to search
pricing: One flat plan: unlimited sourcing, email enrichment, contacts, agents and seats; free to start; paid plan quoted per team (no public price); 10x ROI guarantee (vendor-stated)
overview: Noon is an agentic sourcing tool: you give it a role, it reads the requirements, searches across public and licensed data beyond LinkedIn, ranks candidates against the non-negotiables, verifies contact details, and drafts personalized email and SMS outreach that goes out once the recruiter approves. Replies flow back into the pipeline and synced ATSs. It suits teams that want throughput without adding sourcer headcount, and it is one of the few tools in the category whose unit of value is engaged candidates rather than database access.
pros: End-to-end automation from search to first reply, with approval gates
Multi-channel outreach across email and SMS with no InMail-style credit caps
Transparent, structured candidate evaluation against stated requirements
cons: Newer vendor with a shorter track record than hireEZ or SeekOut
Best fit for outbound-heavy roles; adds little to inbound-heavy hourly hiring
Fewer enterprise admin features than talent-intelligence suites
specs: Candidate search, screening and ranking, contact verification, personalised outreach and follow-up, interview scheduling
Open web plus licensed data, not only LinkedIn profiles
One flat plan, unlimited seats and contacts; free to start; quote-based
40+ including Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Workable, Bullhorn, iCIMS, Loxo, Gem, Recruiterflow, Workday
SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, annual penetration test, SSO/SAML, data residency options
Staffing agencies, lean in-house teams, startups, high-volume professional hiring
longOverview: Noon is built around one idea: the recruiter should not have to run the search. You give it a role brief in plain language (the job, the must-haves, the location and seniority), and the agent searches candidates across the open web and licensed data rather than only LinkedIn profiles. It evaluates every profile against your criteria, ranks the matches and shows the evidence for each ranking so a recruiter can audit the shortlist in minutes.

Calibration is what makes the shortlists improve. Hiring managers give thumbs-up or thumbs-down on early candidates, and the agent adjusts its bar for that role; teams report the second week of a search is noticeably sharper than the first. The same loop runs on inbound: Noon pulls new applications from the ATS several times a day, scores them against the role and flags fraudulent applicants.

Outreach is personalised and runs on two channels, email and SMS. Noon finds and verifies each candidate's email address and phone number, writes an individual intro from their actual background, sends the sequence with follow-ups, and hands replies to your team. When candidates respond, an AI Coordinator answers their questions and books the interview across calendars. Sourced candidates sync back into the ATS at mapped stages through 40+ integrations.

Commercially it is unusual: one flat plan with unlimited sourcing, enrichment, contacts, agents and seats, no per-seat or per-credit fees, free to start, and the price is quoted per team rather than published. Noon states a 10x ROI guarantee. It is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant with annual third-party penetration testing, SSO/SAML and data residency options. It is based in New York and reports 4,000+ recruiting teams using the product.

faq.q: Is Noon the best recruiting tool?
faq.a: It is our #1 recruitment tool for 2026 and the top sourcing tool in this guide. The reason is simple: every other tool in the stack organises work (tracking, scheduling, notes), while Noon removes the most expensive manual work (finding and contacting candidates) by doing it itself, on one flat plan that is free to start. Pair it with an ATS such as Ashby or Greenhouse.

faq.q: Does Noon contact candidates on LinkedIn?
faq.a: No. Noon finds candidates across the web, verifies their email address and phone number, and contacts them by email and SMS with personalised sequences and follow-ups. It does not send LinkedIn messages or InMail.

Noon is free to start. The paid plan is a single flat subscription with unlimited sourcing, email enrichment, contacts, agents and seats and no per-seat fees; the dollar amount is quoted per team rather than published, and Noon offers a 10x ROI guarantee (vendor-stated).

faq.q: Which ATS does Noon integrate with?
faq.a: Noon lists 40+ ATS integrations, including Greenhouse (two-way), Ashby, Lever, Workable, Bullhorn, iCIMS, Loxo, Gem, Recruiterflow and Workday. Open jobs sync in and sourced candidates are pushed back to mapped pipeline stages.

name: hireEZ
tagline: Outbound recruiting platform with an 800M+ profile database and AI sourcing.
bestFor: In-house TA teams running high-volume outbound sourcing with ATS integration needs
pricing: Solo plan published from about $494 per month; team and enterprise plans quote-based.
overview: hireEZ (formerly Hiretual) aggregates public profiles from LinkedIn, GitHub, and dozens of other sources into one searchable database with contact finding, AI matching, sequenced outreach, and deep ATS integrations. Recent releases emphasise agentic features that build searches from job descriptions.
pros: Very large aggregated database with strong contact coverage
Mature ATS integrations including Workday and iCIMS
cons: Team pricing is quote-based and expensive for small teams

name: SeekOut
tagline: Talent intelligence platform with deep diversity and technical filters.
bestFor: Enterprise TA teams prioritising diversity sourcing and internal talent rediscovery
pricing: Quote-based; enterprise contracts typically five figures per year and up.
overview: SeekOut combines an 800M+ profile index with diversity filters, technical signals (GitHub, patents, papers), security-clearance search, and an internal-talent module that mines the existing workforce and ATS. It is a favourite of large tech and defence employers.
pros: Internal mobility and ATS rediscovery module
cons: Outreach features thinner than CRM-first competitors

name: Gem
tagline: Sourcing extension, outreach sequences, and CRM analytics for in-house teams.
bestFor: Tech and mid-market TA teams that want sourcing and nurture analytics on top of Greenhouse or Lever
pricing: Quote-based; published small-team pricing introduced in 2025, mid-market deals typically $15,000–$60,000 per year.
overview: Gem started as a Chrome extension that captured LinkedIn profiles and automated email sequences; it has grown into a full recruiting CRM with talent pools, event workflows, AI sourcing, and the most-used pipeline analytics layer for Greenhouse and Lever customers. In 2025 it added its own ATS.
cons: Database is smaller than hireEZ/SeekOut; relies on LinkedIn browsing
Now competes with the ATSs it integrates with

name: Juicebox (PeopleGPT)
tagline: Natural-language people search over 800M+ profiles.
bestFor: Recruiters and founders who want to describe a candidate in plain English and get a ranked list fast
pricing: Published self-serve plans from roughly $79 per month; team plans quote-based.
overview: Juicebox's PeopleGPT lets you type a description ('staff backend engineers who have worked at a Series B fintech and know Go') and returns ranked profiles with reasoning, plus contact data and outreach. It is the easiest AI search on the market; depth of workflow is still catching up.
pros: Fastest natural-language search in the category
Transparent self-serve pricing with a free trial
cons: Contact credits consumed quickly at volume

name: LinkedIn Recruiter
tagline: The largest professional network's sourcing seat, with InMail and Hiring Assistant AI.
bestFor: Teams with budget that need the broadest active professional reach
pricing: Recruiter Lite from about $170 per month; full Recruiter seats roughly $10,000+ per seat per year at list price.
overview: LinkedIn Recruiter remains the reference sourcing tool because of its network size and activity signals (open-to-work, recent updates). InMail credits, seat pricing, and LinkedIn's limits on third-party automation are the main complaints; the Hiring Assistant AI agent now automates search and messaging inside LinkedIn's walls.
pros: Hiring Assistant adds agentic search and messaging
ATS integrations via Recruiter System Connect
cons: InMail caps and declining response rates
No email or phone data without additional tools

name: Fetcher
tagline: AI sourcing with human curation and automated email outreach.
bestFor: Small and mid-sized teams that want a steady flow of vetted candidates without doing the searching
pricing: Quote-based subscriptions per active role or seat; published starter tiers in the low hundreds per month.
overview: Fetcher pairs AI search with a human review layer and delivers batches of candidates with verified emails and automated sequences. It is a good fit for teams that want sourcing as a service rather than another search interface.
cons: Less control over search than database tools
Batch cadence slower than real-time search
Smaller database coverage in some regions

name: Findem
tagline: Attribute-based talent search built from 3D career data.
bestFor: Enterprise teams that want sourcing, rediscovery, and talent analytics in one platform
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts.
overview: Findem builds 'attributes' (inferred facts like 'scaled a team from 10 to 100' or 'built a payments product') from career histories and lets recruiters search on them instead of keywords. It also runs ATS rediscovery and inbound ranking, making it a full talent-intelligence layer.
pros: Attribute search finds people keyword search misses
Strong ATS rediscovery and inbound ranking
cons: Attribute inference needs validation on niche roles

name: SourceWhale
tagline: Outreach sequencing and contact finding built for agency recruiters.
bestFor: Staffing and search firms that live in Bullhorn and need multichannel sequences
pricing: Per-user subscriptions, typically $100–$200 per user per month on annual terms.
overview: SourceWhale layers contact finding, sequencing, and reply tracking on top of agency CRMs like Bullhorn, Vincere, and JobAdder. It is widely used by UK and US recruiting agencies for business development as well as candidate outreach.
pros: Business-development and candidate workflows in one tool
cons: Not a talent database; relies on where you browse
Per-user cost adds up for large agencies
In-house teams find agency focus distracting

name: Beamery
tagline: Enterprise talent CRM and skills-based talent lifecycle platform.
bestFor: Large enterprises running talent marketing, events, and internal mobility programs
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts, generally six figures per year.
overview: Beamery is an enterprise CRM that extends into skills intelligence, internal mobility, and career sites. It suits organisations with dedicated talent-marketing teams; smaller companies will find it heavy.
pros: Strong integrations with Workday and SAP

name: Avature
tagline: Highly configurable enterprise CRM, ATS, and event platform.
bestFor: Global enterprises that need bespoke workflows and campus/event recruiting at scale
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts.
overview: Avature is the most configurable platform in the category: nearly any workflow can be modelled, which is why many Fortune 500 companies use it for campus, events, contingent, and executive programs. That flexibility comes with a steep admin learning curve.
pros: Strong campus and event recruiting modules

name: Phenom
tagline: AI career sites, CRM, and chatbot for enterprise talent marketing.
bestFor: Enterprises that want a personalised career site and chatbot feeding the CRM
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts.
overview: Phenom's strength is the front door: AI-personalised career sites, a conversational chatbot, and automated job matching, all wired into a CRM and campaign engine. It is commonly layered on top of Workday or iCIMS.
pros: Chatbot and automated scheduling reduce recruiter load
cons: Dependent on the underlying ATS for pipeline

name: Sense
tagline: Candidate engagement automation (text, email, chatbot) for staffing and high-volume teams.
bestFor: Staffing agencies and high-volume employers that need automated texting and redeployment
pricing: Quote-based; priced per recruiter or per contact volume.
overview: Sense automates candidate communication across SMS, email, and a chatbot, with journeys for application nudges, onboarding, check-ins, and redeployment. It integrates tightly with Bullhorn and staffing ATSs and is widely used in healthcare and light-industrial staffing.
pros: Redeployment and NPS journeys built for staffing

name: Paradox (Olivia)
tagline: Conversational recruiting assistant that screens, schedules, and texts candidates.
bestFor: High-volume hourly and frontline hiring (retail, QSR, logistics, healthcare)
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts, often priced per location or hire volume.
overview: Paradox's assistant, Olivia, handles the conversation layer of high-volume hiring: text-to-apply, screening questions, interview scheduling, reminders, and onboarding paperwork, in dozens of languages. Many large frontline employers report time-to-hire dropping from weeks to days.
pros: Dramatic time-to-hire reduction for hourly roles
Deep Workday, SAP, and iCIMS integrations
cons: Less relevant for professional, low-volume hiring

name: GoodTime
tagline: Interview scheduling automation for high-volume and panel-heavy teams.
bestFor: Mid-market and enterprise TA teams scheduling hundreds of interviews a week
pricing: Quote-based; typically $10,000–$50,000+ per year depending on volume.
overview: GoodTime automates complex loops: interviewer pools with load limits and training tracks, candidate self-scheduling, room booking, and rescheduling, with analytics on coordinator time and interviewer burden. It integrates with Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, and most calendars.
cons: Overlaps with native ATS scheduling for simple needs

name: Prelude by Calendly
tagline: Recruiting-specific scheduling now folded into Calendly.
bestFor: Teams already on Calendly that need panel scheduling and ATS sync
pricing: Calendly Teams/Enterprise plans; recruiting features quote-based.
overview: Calendly acquired Prelude in 2022 and has merged its panel and loop scheduling into Calendly's enterprise tiers, giving recruiting teams ATS integrations and round-robin interviewer pools on a familiar product.
cons: Less specialised than GoodTime for complex loops

name: ModernLoop
tagline: Scheduling and interviewer training built for tech recruiting loops.
bestFor: Tech companies with structured interview loops and interviewer certification programs
pricing: Quote-based, generally mid five figures per year.
overview: ModernLoop focuses on engineering-style loops: automated panel composition, shadow/reverse-shadow training, debrief scheduling, and a candidate portal. It is popular with Series B–D tech companies on Greenhouse or Ashby.
pros: Fast loop scheduling with conflict resolution

name: Cal.com
tagline: Open-source scheduling with free individual plans and round-robin teams.
bestFor: Small teams and agencies that want free or self-hosted booking links
pricing: Free individual plan; Teams from about $15 per user per month; self-host option.
overview: Cal.com is the open-source Calendly alternative: booking pages, round-robin and collective events, and integrations with calendars and video tools. It is not a recruiting scheduler but covers screens and simple panels at near-zero cost.
cons: No interviewer training or load analytics

name: HackerRank
tagline: Technical screening and interview platform with the largest question library.
bestFor: Companies hiring software engineers at volume who need proctored screens and live interviews
pricing: Published starter plans from about $165 per month; enterprise quote-based, often $50,000+ per year.
overview: HackerRank offers coding screens, project-based assessments, live interview pads, and AI-assisted plagiarism detection, plus a large developer community that keeps the question bank fresh. It is the most widely adopted technical screening tool at enterprise scale.
pros: Largest library of role-based technical questions
cons: Non-technical assessments are not a focus

name: CodeSignal
tagline: Validated technical assessments with a standardised coding score.
bestFor: Teams that want a defensible, comparable technical score across candidates
pricing: Quote-based; enterprise contracts commonly five to six figures per year.
overview: CodeSignal's General Coding Assessment produces a standardised score many companies accept in place of their own screen, plus realistic IDE-based assessments and live interview tooling. Its validation research is among the most rigorous in the category.
pros: Shared-score programs reduce repeat testing for candidates

name: Codility
tagline: Technical hiring assessments popular with European and global enterprises.
bestFor: Global engineering teams that need multilingual, anti-cheating technical screens
pricing: Published starter plans from roughly $1,200 per year; enterprise quote-based.
overview: Codility (CodeCheck, CodeLive) is a long-standing technical assessment vendor with strong anti-cheating controls, a wide language set, and competitive published starter pricing. It is especially common in Europe.
cons: Smaller community and question library than HackerRank
Live interview tool is adequate, not exceptional

name: TestGorilla
tagline: Library of 400+ skills, personality, and cognitive tests for all roles.
bestFor: Small and mid-sized companies screening non-technical roles at volume
pricing: Free plan with limited tests; paid plans from roughly $75 per month.
overview: TestGorilla lets you combine multiple short tests (skills, cognitive, personality, language, culture add) into one assessment candidates complete in under an hour. It is the most accessible general-purpose assessment tool and has a usable free tier.
cons: Validity varies across tests; review before using as a hard screen

name: Vervoe
tagline: AI-graded job simulations and skills tests.
bestFor: High-volume non-technical hiring where realistic work samples beat resumes
pricing: Published plans from about $300 per month; enterprise quote-based.
overview: Vervoe builds realistic job simulations (customer emails, spreadsheets, sales calls) and uses AI grading to rank candidates on actual performance. It suits roles where portfolios do not exist and resumes are weak predictors.
pros: AI grading scales to high volume

name: HireVue
tagline: Enterprise video interviewing, assessments, and conversational AI.
bestFor: Large employers running thousands of one-way video screens and structured interviews
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts, commonly $35,000+ per year.
overview: HireVue is the enterprise standard for one-way video interviews, game-based and coding assessments, interview scheduling, and a text-based recruiting assistant. It has invested heavily in fairness audits after earlier controversy over facial analysis, which it discontinued.
pros: Scales to very high interview volumes
cons: Candidate perceptions of one-way video vary

name: Spark Hire
tagline: Affordable one-way and live video interviewing for small and mid-sized teams.
bestFor: Companies of 20–1,000 employees replacing phone screens with recorded interviews
pricing: Published plans from about $149 per month; higher tiers add users and features.
overview: Spark Hire offers one-way video questions, live interviews, interview scheduling, and reference checks (via its Comeet and Chally acquisitions) at published prices far below HireVue. It integrates with most small-business and mid-market ATS products.
cons: Branding and customisation limited on lower tiers
Not designed for very high enterprise volumes

name: BrightHire
tagline: Interview intelligence: recording, transcription, AI notes, and interviewer coaching.
bestFor: Teams that want consistent interview feedback and coaching without a dedicated video platform
pricing: Quote-based; typically priced per interviewer, mid five figures per year for mid-market teams.
overview: BrightHire joins your Zoom, Meet, or Teams interviews, records and transcribes them, drafts scorecard notes, and surfaces coaching insights such as talk ratio and question consistency. It plugs into the ATS so notes land on the candidate record.
cons: Candidate consent and recording policies required

name: Metaview
tagline: AI note-taker purpose-built for recruiter screens and interviews.
bestFor: Recruiters who want automatic intake and screen notes written in the ATS's format
pricing: Free tier for individuals; team plans from roughly $50 per user per month.
overview: Metaview records calls and writes structured notes tailored to recruiting: intake summaries, screen notes mapped to scorecard fields, and candidate summaries pushed to Greenhouse, Ashby, or Lever. Its free tier makes it one of the easiest AI tools to adopt.

name: Checkr
tagline: API-first background checks with fast turnaround and strong ATS integrations.
bestFor: Tech-forward companies and gig platforms that want automated, integrated screening
pricing: Pay-per-check from about $30 (basic) to $80+ (professional) per candidate; volume pricing available.
overview: Checkr modernised background checks with an API, a candidate-friendly mobile flow, and integrations into nearly every ATS and HRIS. It is the default for startups and marketplaces, and has expanded into continuous monitoring and international checks.
pros: Fast turnaround and clear candidate status
cons: International coverage less deep than Sterling/HireRight
Support experience varies at low volumes

name: Sterling
tagline: Global enterprise screening and identity verification (now part of First Advantage).
bestFor: Enterprises with multi-country hiring and regulated-industry requirements
pricing: Quote-based; per-check pricing negotiated on volume.
overview: Sterling runs background checks, drug testing, and identity verification in 240+ countries and territories, with deep integrations into enterprise ATSs. First Advantage acquired it in 2024, creating one of the largest screening providers.
cons: Candidate experience less polished than Checkr

name: HireRight
tagline: Global background screening for large employers.
bestFor: Multinational enterprises and transport/healthcare employers
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts.
overview: HireRight provides employment, criminal, education, drug, and driving-record screening worldwide, with strong presence in transportation and healthcare. It competes directly with Sterling and First Advantage for global programs.
cons: Turnaround and support can lag at volume

name: GoodHire
tagline: Small-business background checks with published pricing (a Checkr company).
bestFor: Small businesses running a handful of checks per month
pricing: Published packages from about $30 to $80+ per check with no subscription.
overview: GoodHire packages FCRA-compliant checks for small businesses with transparent pricing, a simple portal, and built-in adverse-action tooling. Checkr acquired it in 2022; it remains the SMB-friendly brand.
cons: Volume buyers should go direct to Checkr

name: Indeed
tagline: The largest job site; free organic posts plus sponsored and resume-database products.
bestFor: Any inbound-heavy hiring, especially hourly and local roles
pricing: Free organic listings; sponsored jobs priced per click or per application with a daily budget; Indeed Resume subscriptions from about $120 per month.
overview: Indeed remains the highest-volume source of applicants in most markets. Sponsored posts, Indeed Apply, screener questions, and the resume database make it the first distribution channel to configure in any ATS; its Smart Sourcing AI adds candidate matching.
pros: Largest applicant volume in most geographies
Easy apply and screener questions integrated with ATSs
cons: Sponsored costs rise for competitive roles

name: LinkedIn Jobs
tagline: Professional-network job posts with strong reach for knowledge-worker roles.
bestFor: Professional, technical, and management roles
pricing: One free post at a time; promoted posts on a daily budget; Job Slots on contract.
overview: LinkedIn's job posts reach a professional audience and benefit from network effects (employee shares, 'open to work' matching). Promoted posts can be expensive for competitive roles, and the apply flow favours LinkedIn's own forms.
cons: Applicant quality mixed for high-visibility roles
Hourly and frontline reach weaker than Indeed

name: ZipRecruiter
tagline: One post distributed to 100+ boards with AI candidate matching.
bestFor: Small and mid-sized businesses that want broad distribution without managing boards
pricing: Published plans from about $299 per month per job (Standard) with a free trial; higher tiers add features and reach.
overview: ZipRecruiter syndicates a posting to its partner network and uses matching technology to invite likely candidates to apply, which makes it a time-saver for small teams. Its costs per job are higher than organic Indeed but include distribution.
cons: Less effective for niche professional roles

name: Appcast
tagline: Programmatic job advertising that optimises spend toward applications.
bestFor: High-volume employers and agencies spending five figures or more a month on job ads
pricing: Percentage of media spend or cost-per-application pricing; minimum spend requirements.
overview: Appcast buys sponsored placements across thousands of boards and shifts budget automatically toward sources producing applications at target cost, with rules per role and location. It is the largest programmatic job-ad platform and publishes useful benchmark data.
cons: Requires meaningful ad spend to justify
Less relevant for low-volume professional hiring
Attribution depends on ATS tracking setup

name: Rippling
tagline: HRIS, payroll, IT, and onboarding in one system with a built-in ATS.
bestFor: Companies of 20–2,000 employees that want hiring data to flow straight into payroll and device provisioning
pricing: Modular per-employee pricing; core platform from about $8 per employee per month plus modules.
overview: Rippling unifies employee data across HR, payroll, benefits, IT (devices, apps) and now recruiting, so a new hire's offer acceptance can trigger payroll setup, laptop shipment, and app access automatically. Its onboarding workflows are among the most complete available.
pros: Onboarding triggers IT and payroll automatically
Includes a capable ATS for small companies
cons: Breadth means some modules are shallower than specialists

name: BambooHR
tagline: Small-business HRIS with built-in ATS, onboarding, and e-signature.
bestFor: Companies of 25–500 employees that want simple HR and onboarding together
pricing: Per-employee monthly pricing in two tiers (Core and Pro); quote generated online.
overview: BambooHR pairs an approachable HRIS with an ATS, onboarding checklists, e-signature, and new-hire packets. It is a frequent first HR system for growing companies and integrates with most small-business recruiting tools.
pros: Large integration marketplace for its segment
cons: ATS is basic compared with dedicated products

name: HiBob
tagline: Modern HRIS with culture-focused onboarding for mid-sized global companies.
bestFor: Distributed mid-market companies that want onboarding tied to engagement and culture
pricing: Quote-based per-employee pricing.
overview: HiBob's 'bob' platform emphasises people experience: onboarding flows with buddies and surveys, org charts, compensation, and performance. It integrates with Greenhouse, Ashby, and other ATSs and is popular with international scale-ups.

name: Enboarder
tagline: Human-centric onboarding journeys for large employers.
bestFor: Enterprises that want preboarding and onboarding experiences beyond paperwork
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts.
overview: Enboarder designs mobile-first onboarding journeys that nudge managers, buddies, and new hires with timed content and tasks, layered on top of the HRIS. It is used by large employers to reduce early attrition.
pros: Manager and buddy engagement built in

name: Gem Insights
tagline: Pipeline, passthrough, and DE&I analytics layered on Greenhouse and Lever.
bestFor: Tech TA teams on Greenhouse or Lever that need better funnel and forecast reporting
pricing: Included with Gem CRM tiers or sold as a module; quote-based.
overview: Gem's analytics layer turns ATS data into passthrough rates, forecasts, recruiter capacity, and DE&I funnels without a warehouse project. It is the most common first analytics add-on for Greenhouse and Lever customers.
pros: Fast time to insight on Greenhouse/Lever data

name: Ashby Analytics
tagline: Report builder and dashboards included with the Ashby ATS.
bestFor: Teams on Ashby that would otherwise buy a separate analytics tool
pricing: Included with Ashby ATS plans.
overview: Ashby's native analytics let teams build custom reports on any field, track goals and capacity, and share dashboards with hiring managers, which is a major reason companies switch to the ATS. It only reports on Ashby data.
cons: Cross-system (HRIS) analysis still needs a warehouse

name: Visier
tagline: Enterprise people analytics spanning talent acquisition and workforce planning.
bestFor: Large enterprises that want TA metrics inside a broader people-analytics platform
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts, typically six figures per year.
overview: Visier connects ATS, HRIS, and finance data into pre-built people-analytics models (including talent-acquisition funnels, source quality, and quality-of-hire) with benchmarks across its customer base. It is a people-analytics platform first and a recruiting tool second.
pros: Connects hiring to retention and performance outcomes

name: Noon Inbound Screening
tagline: Criteria-based screening of inbound applicants, synced both ways with the ATS.
bestFor: Teams on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable or Loxo that want every applicant evaluated against the role's actual criteria, with the decision written back to the ATS stage
pricing: Included in Noon's single team plan with unlimited seats, quoted per team; not sold separately.
overview: Noon pulls inbound applications from the connected ATS several times a day, evaluates each one against the role's criteria and non-negotiables with a reason per criterion, and ranks the queue. Advance and reject decisions sync back to mapped ATS stages with the ATS's own rejection reasons. Hiring-manager feedback recalibrates the weighting per role, and changing the criteria re-ranks everyone already in the queue. It is the same evaluation engine Noon uses for outbound sourcing, applied to applicants; it does not run outreach on inbound roles.
pros: Evaluation against written criteria with evidence, not a similarity score
Two-way sync with the ATS, including rejection reasons
Re-ranks the whole queue when criteria change
Shares one team plan with Noon's sourcing, interviewer and fraud tools
cons: Requires one of the supported ATSs; no standalone applicant inbox
Newer than the enterprise matching suites
Screening quality depends on how specific the role criteria are

name: Eightfold Talent Intelligence
tagline: Enterprise talent intelligence that matches, ranks and rediscovers candidates at scale.
bestFor: Large enterprises that want one matching model across applicants, internal mobility and the existing talent pool
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts; typically six figures a year.
overview: Eightfold applies a skills-based matching model across every candidate a company has ever seen: new applicants, past applicants and current employees. It ranks applicants against roles, infers adjacent skills, and powers career sites and internal mobility from the same model. It is a platform decision rather than a tool purchase, with the implementation effort and price to match.
pros: Skills inference that goes well beyond keyword matching
One model across applicants, alumni and employees
Mature enterprise security and audit controls
cons: Matching logic is less transparent to the end recruiter than criteria-based tools

name: Harver
tagline: Volume-hiring assessments and matching for frontline and contact-centre roles.
bestFor: Retail, logistics, hospitality and contact-centre employers screening thousands of applicants a month
pricing: Quote-based; priced on application volume with annual contracts.
overview: Harver (which absorbed pymetrics and Outmatch) screens high-volume applicants with short assessments, realistic job previews and automated matching, then routes qualified people straight to scheduling. It is built for roles where the application is thin and the predictive signal comes from the assessment rather than the CV.
pros: Assessment-based screening suits roles with thin CVs
Realistic job previews cut early attrition
cons: Assessment-first flow is wrong for senior and specialist roles
Volume pricing is expensive for small employers
Several merged products with uneven user experience

name: Textkernel
tagline: CV parsing and semantic matching embedded in ATSs and staffing platforms.
bestFor: Staffing firms and ATS vendors that need high-accuracy parsing and matching inside an existing system
pricing: Quote-based, usually priced per parsed document or per seat; often bundled by the ATS vendor.
overview: Textkernel is the parsing and matching engine behind many ATS and staffing products rather than a recruiter-facing application in its own right. It parses CVs and job descriptions in many languages, normalises skills and titles to a taxonomy, and matches candidates to jobs and jobs to candidates. Staffing agencies buy it to search their own database; ATS vendors embed it.
pros: Skills and title taxonomy that makes search consistent
Embedded in many staffing platforms already
cons: Infrastructure, not a workflow: no screening decisions or ATS write-back of its own
Value depends on the host system
Little use to in-house teams without a large candidate database

name: Noon AI Interviewer
tagline: Voice AI that runs first-round screens on the team's own questions, on the candidate's schedule.
bestFor: Teams that want every qualified applicant or sourced candidate screened within a day without adding recruiter phone-screen capacity
pricing: Included in Noon's single team plan with unlimited seats, quoted per team; not sold separately.
overview: Candidates receive an email link and start the interview whenever they are ready. The AI conducts a live voice conversation asking the role-specific questions the team defined, with configurable duration, voice and link expiry, and a sandbox mode for testing the script. The team receives a full transcript, a structured analysis against the questions, and a next-round recommendation. It is a voice screen, not a video interview, and it is one component of Noon's recruiting platform alongside sourcing, inbound screening and the notetaker.
pros: Candidate chooses the time; no scheduling step
Role-specific questions set by the team, not a generic bank
Transcript plus structured analysis and recommendation
Included in the team plan with Noon's other tools
cons: Not sold without the rest of the Noon platform
Voice only; no video or coding assessment
Shorter track record than the volume-hiring specialists

name: Sapia.ai
tagline: Chat-based structured interviews with explainable scoring for volume hiring.
bestFor: Large employers in retail, hospitality and financial services running thousands of first-round screens
pricing: Quote-based enterprise contracts, priced on hiring volume.
overview: Sapia runs an untimed, text-based structured interview that candidates complete on their phone, scores the answers against a validated competency model, and gives every candidate personalised feedback. It publishes its fairness testing and is one of the more mature products on bias documentation, which matters for employers under NYC Local Law 144 or EU AI Act obligations.
pros: Every candidate gets feedback, which protects employer brand at volume
Text format is accessible and low-pressure
cons: Built for volume; expensive for small teams
Competency model takes configuration per role family

name: micro1
tagline: AI interviewer for technical screening, paired with a vetted engineering talent pool.
bestFor: Companies screening software engineers at volume, or hiring from micro1's pre-vetted pool
pricing: Quote-based; the interviewer is also offered as part of micro1's talent marketplace.
overview: micro1's interviewer conducts a conversational technical screen, including follow-up questions on the candidate's answers and a coding component, and returns a scored report. The company also runs a marketplace of engineers who have already passed it, so some buyers use the interviewer and others buy the pre-screened pool.
pros: Technical follow-up questions rather than a fixed script
Coding assessment built into the conversation
cons: Fewer ATS integrations than established vendors
Dual marketplace model can blur the vendor relationship

name: Apriora
tagline: Real-time AI interviewer that conducts live video and voice screens.
bestFor: Teams that want a live, conversational first-round screen with scheduling handled by the tool
pricing: Quote-based; per-interview and per-role plans reported.
overview: Apriora's interviewer, Alex, runs a live two-way conversation, adapts follow-ups to the candidate's answers, and returns a transcript, scorecard and recommendation. It targets the same first-round screen as the other tools here and differentiates on the realism of the live conversation.
pros: Live conversation that feels closer to a human screen
Scorecard mapped to the role's requirements
cons: Live format means candidates must book a time, unlike asynchronous tools

name: Noon AI Notetaker
tagline: Interview notetaker that tracks whether the planned questions actually got asked.
bestFor: Teams whose hiring managers interview occasionally and need the plan kept on track, with notes landing beside the sourcing and screening record
pricing: Included in Noon's single team plan with unlimited seats, quoted per team; not sold separately.
overview: Noon's notetaker joins live interview meetings such as Google Meet as a participant, records and transcribes with speaker labels, and produces a post-meeting summary. Its distinctive feature is coverage tracking: the team sets the questions the interview is expected to cover, and the notetaker tracks which were asked and reminds the interviewer about the ones missed. It sits alongside Noon's sourcing, inbound screening and AI interviewer on the same candidate record.
pros: Coverage tracking against pre-set expected questions
Notes live with the candidate's sourcing and screening history
cons: Not sold without the rest of the Noon platform
Meeting-platform coverage narrower than general notetakers

name: Fireflies.ai
tagline: General meeting notetaker with transcription, summaries and searchable call history.
bestFor: Small teams that want one notetaker for interviews and every other meeting, with a free tier to start
pricing: Free tier with limited transcription credits; paid plans from roughly $10–$20 per seat per month, enterprise on quote.
overview: Fireflies joins Zoom, Meet and Teams calls, transcribes, summarises and makes every meeting searchable. It is not built for recruiting, so there is no scorecard mapping or question coverage, but the price and the breadth of integrations make it the default for teams that interview occasionally.
pros: Free tier and low paid price
cons: No recruiting structure: scorecards and coverage have to be rebuilt by hand
Candidate-consent flow is the generic recording notice

name: Otter.ai
tagline: Real-time transcription and meeting notes with a generous free plan.
bestFor: Individuals and small teams that want live transcription during interviews at the lowest cost
pricing: Free plan with monthly transcription minutes; Pro from roughly $17 per user per month, Business from roughly $30.
overview: Otter transcribes live, so the interviewer can see the transcript appear during the conversation, and produces a summary and action items afterwards. Like Fireflies it has no recruiting-specific structure; it wins on real-time transcription and price.
pros: Simple to adopt for one interviewer

name: tl;dv
tagline: Meeting recorder with AI notes, clips and multi-meeting reports.
bestFor: Teams that want to share interview clips and highlights with hiring managers who were not on the call
pricing: Free plan with limits; paid plans from roughly $20–$30 per seat per month.
overview: tl;dv records and transcribes meetings and is strongest at sharing: timestamped clips, highlight reels and recurring reports across many meetings. For hiring, that makes it useful for showing a hiring manager the three minutes that mattered rather than a 45-minute recording.
cons: Recording-first design can feel intrusive to candidates

name: Noon Fraud Detection
tagline: Layered applicant fraud detection across inbound applications and sourced candidates.
bestFor: Remote-first and high-inbound teams that want fraudulent applicants flagged with the reasons shown, before anyone books an interview
pricing: Included in Noon's single team plan with unlimited seats, quoted per team; not sold separately.
overview: Noon's fraud detection is a layered system that correlates signals across network, identity and location, email and online footprint, rather than applying isolated rules. When the combination looks wrong it raises an explainable flag listing the signals that triggered it, keeps the flag across roles so a reapplying candidate is caught, and leaves the decision to a reviewer. It covers both inbound applicants and candidates Noon finds through sourcing, and runs inside the same platform as the screening and interviewer tools.
pros: Signals correlated across layers, not single-rule rejection
Explainable flags with the triggering signals shown
Persists across roles; reviewer stays in the loop
cons: Not sold standalone outside the Noon platform
No government-ID or liveness verification; pair with an IDV tool at offer stage for regulated roles

name: Persona
tagline: Government-ID and liveness verification for confirming a candidate is who they claim.
bestFor: Regulated or remote employers that need identity verified at offer or onboarding, and platforms vetting contractors
pricing: Usage-based per verification with a free starter tier; enterprise on quote.
overview: Persona verifies identity documents, matches a live selfie to the document, and checks for known fraud patterns. It is a general identity platform rather than a recruiting tool, so teams use it at the offer or onboarding step, or inside a candidate marketplace, rather than at the top of the funnel.
pros: Document and liveness verification that catches impostor candidates
Usage-based pricing scales down to small volumes
cons: Too much friction for top-of-funnel screening
No signal on duplicate or fabricated applications before the ID step
Requires integration work; no native ATS connectors

name: Fama
tagline: AI screening of candidates' online footprint for misconduct and misrepresentation.
bestFor: Employers that want a compliant, consent-based check of a candidate's public online presence before offer
pricing: Per-report pricing with volume tiers; quote-based for enterprise.
overview: Fama screens a candidate's public web and social presence with the candidate's consent, flagging behaviour the employer has defined as relevant and redacting protected-class information so recruiters only see what they are allowed to consider. It is a pre-hire compliance tool; it helps confirm that a footprint exists and matches the application, but it is not designed to detect duplicate or proxy applications.
pros: Redacts protected information from the report
cons: Pre-offer timing; no help at application screening
Per-report pricing adds up at volume
Not built for duplicate-application or proxy-candidate detection

name: Ferretly
tagline: Social media and online background screening for pre-hire checks.
bestFor: Staffing firms and employers adding a consent-based online screen to their existing background-check step
pricing: Per-report pricing; volume and partner plans on quote.
overview: Ferretly produces a consent-based report on a candidate's public social media and web presence, categorised against the behaviours the employer selected, with protected-class content filtered out. Like Fama it is a late-stage compliance check that can corroborate a candidate's claimed footprint rather than a tool for catching fraudulent applications at the top of the funnel.
pros: Consent and compliance handled in the flow
cons: No signal on identity or duplicate applications
